title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: §50 'Exemple : le tour de Fermat' of the continuation of La Longue Marche. Let G0^ be the profinite completion of SL(2,Z). Pi0 is the free subgroup generated by lambda_0 = -l_0 and lambda_1 = -l_1, the loops around the cusps 0 and 1; Pi0 is the (profinite) pi_1 of P^1-{0,1,inf}. Sign conventions follow the previous page: l_0 = sigma rho sigma rho and l_1 = rho sigma rho sigma, with rho of order 6, sigma of order 4 and rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. The group G is (G0, enlarged by an orientation-reversing tau') modulo [Pi0,Pi0]. It is an extension of a finite group H by M = (Pi0)^ab ≅ Z^{0,1,inf}/diagonal (tensored with Z^). This is the abelian, 'Fermat' level of the tower: the finite quotients of M correspond to the Fermat curves x^n+y^n=z^n.

Upper half of the page:
(6) Defines the third cusp generator lambda_inf := -l_inf = rho sigma rho^{-1} sigma rho, rewritten as rho(sigma) sigma rho = -rho sigma(rho)^{-1} rho = rho sigma rho^{-1}(sigma).
(7) States the relation [sigma, lambda_inf] = 1 in G (sigma = sigma_inf is the 'local' involution at the cusp inf). The NB justifies it with two group-theoretic identities in SL2(Z):
- [l_0,l_1] = [lambda_0,lambda_1] = (sigma(rho) rho^{-1})^3;
- [sigma_inf, lambda_inf] = (sigma(rho^{-1}) rho)^3 = int(sigma rho^{-1})·[l_0,l_1].
So the commutator [sigma, lambda_inf] is conjugate to [l_0,l_1]. In the presentation (3) of the previous page, the relation [lambda_0,lambda_1] = 1 can therefore be replaced by the relation [sigma, rho sigma rho^{-1} sigma rho] = 1.

Lower half of the page: the goal is announced, namely to define a group scheme over Spec Z whose Z^-points recover the profinite group G^. One puts M̲ = G̲° = Z^{0,1,inf}/diagonal, viewed as a vector group (V(M), i.e. M⊗G_a). The finite quotient G/M ≅ S_3 × mu_2^± ≅ T_{0,3} ≅ G_{0,3}/Pi (the extended Teichmüller/modular group of type (0,3)) is made to act on M̲.
- The images lambda_0, lambda_1, lambda_inf lie in M̲(Z) ⊂ M̲(Z^) and satisfy lambda_0 + lambda_1 + lambda_inf = 0.
- S_3 acts by permuting the cusps: sigma swaps lambda_0 and lambda_1 and hence fixes lambda_inf; rho cycles lambda_i -> lambda_{i+1}.
- tau = tau_inf = sigma tau' acts by -1.
The next page completes the construction. It builds an extension 1 -> V(M) -> E̲ -> H_Z -> 1 of the constant group scheme H_Z by the vector group. Its 'diagonal' A-points form the pushout of G along M -> M⊗A, and E̲^Δ(Z^) ≅ G^. In effect this is an integral, schematic model of the metabelian/Fermat quotient of the profinite modular group, presumably intended to carry the Galois action.
errors: Orientation slip in the definition of lambda_inf. Using only rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1 one checks rho sigma rho^{-1} sigma rho = -rho sigma rho^2 sigma rho = (rho sigma rho sigma)(sigma rho sigma rho) = l_1 l_0 = lambda_1 lambda_0. With lambda_inf as written on top of the page one gets lambda_inf = lambda_0 + lambda_1 in M, not lambda_0 + lambda_1 + lambda_inf = 0 as claimed in the lower (6). An explicit matrix check (rho = [[1,1],[-1,0]], sigma = [[0,-1],[1,0]]) also gives rho(l_1) = l_inf^{-1}. So for both the zero-sum relation and the cyclic action rho(lambda_i) = lambda_{i+1}, lambda_inf must be replaced by its inverse. The relation [sigma, lambda_inf] = 1 is unaffected.
Related sign slip on the previous page: -sigma rho sigma rho = sigma(rho) rho, not sigma(rho) rho^4 (sigma rho sigma rho itself equals sigma(rho) rho^4 because sigma^2 = rho^3).

[sigma, lambda_inf] = 1 holds only in G, i.e. modulo [Pi0,Pi0], not in SL2(Z). There, an order-4 element cannot commute with a parabolic one. This is consistent with the NB, which shows the commutator is conjugate to [l_0,l_1].

Possible order inconsistency in (5). Modulo M, <sigma,rho> already gives the dicyclic group of order 12 (sigma rho sigma^{-1} ≡ rho^{-1}, sigma^2 = rho^3 central of order 2), and adjoining tau' gives order 24. S_3 × mu_2 has order 12 and no element of order 4. Unless the notation G_3, mu_2^± or the meaning of G here differ (e.g. -1 being factored out), the identification G/M ≅ S_3 × mu_2^± ≅ T_{0,3} needs correction (unsure).

ideas.what: Abelianization M of pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) as Z^{0,1,inf}/diagonal, with the induced action of the modular group quotient S_3 (× ±1) permuting cusps; first level of the 'Fermat tower'
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower / H_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere with S_3 × Z/2 action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; the Galois action on the Fermat tower is studied by Ihara (1986, Annals) and Anderson
ideas.where_published: Fermat curves are discussed in the dessins context of Esquisse d'un programme (unsure of this specific treatment)

ideas.what: Identities [l_0,l_1] = (sigma(rho)rho^{-1})^3 and [sigma, lambda_inf] = int(sigma rho^{-1})[l_0,l_1], giving an alternative presentation of SL2(Z)/[Pi0,Pi0] with the relation [sigma, rho sigma rho^{-1} sigma rho] = 1 instead of [lambda_0,lambda_1] = 1
ideas.modern_name: presentation of the metabelian quotient of the modular group by elliptic generators

ideas.what: Model the profinite group G^ (finite-by-abelian) as the Z^-points of a group scheme over Spec Z: an extension of the constant group H by the vector group V(M) = M⊗G_a, via pushout along M -> M⊗A
ideas.modern_name: integral algebraic hull / pushout extension by a vector group; analogous to (relative) unipotent completion in its abelian truncation
ideas.usually_credited_to: relative and weighted completion: Hain, Hain–Matsumoto; motivic pi_1 over Z: Deligne 1989 (as analogues)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to give the Fermat (abelian) level of the profinite modular tower an arithmetic-geometric incarnation: a group scheme E̲ over Spec Z, an extension of the constant group S_3 × ±1 (resp. H) by the vector group M⊗G_a, whose Z^-points recover G^. This is apparently a first step towards treating the levels of the tower as group schemes over Z on which Galois/cyclotomic actions become algebraic. The page breaks off ('gêné aux entournures'), and the construction is only sketched on the next page.
missed.quote: On va définir un[e] [schéma en groupes] ... sur Z, dans lequel seront les pts de G^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This resembles in spirit, but differs in detail from, the relative/weighted completions of SL2(Z) (Hain, Hain–Matsumoto), which live over Q or Q_l rather than as Z-models of finite-by-abelian quotients. An integral version, extended to the metabelian (Ihara) level, would be a curiosity for those studying Galois actions on the Fermat tower. In this abelian truncation, however, the construction itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine group-theoretic bookkeeping, and it contains a sign/orientation slip in lambda_inf. The one notable element is the announced idea of an integral group-scheme model whose Z^-points are the profinite Fermat-level quotient of the modular group. It is mildly interesting historically as an anticipation of 'algebraic completion' viewpoints, but at this level it is elementary, and it is incomplete on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 probably reads 's'écrit [aussi], en introduisant' rather than 'j'écrit ... introduisant'.
'On va définir une solution [?]' is likely 'On va définir un schéma en groupes [?] ... sur Z, dans lequel seront les pts de G^'. The next page refers to 'L'extension E̲ annoncée'.
'E^{0,1,inf}' in (8) is most likely a (blackboard) Z overwritten: M̲ = G̲° = Z^{0,1,inf}/diagonale.
'M̲(Z^) = M⊗Z' should read M̲(Z^) = M⊗Ẑ (resp. M_Z ⊗ Ẑ).
Left margin near (8): 'Il va falloir noter M̲ ... G̲° !' (a note on notation).
Bottom-left margin: 'ceci se voit directement pour i=0,1, et s'en déduit pour i=inf'.
